wars.note: Called the Anglo-Bhutan War on the Raj page ('A war was fought in 1864-1865 (the Anglo-Bhutan Duar War)'). The Duar War page: 'a war fought between British India and Bhutan in 1864 to 1865', 'lasted only five months'. Repair sa-06-d: zones were empty although ground changed hands (reviewer); the zone is the one in the kingdom-of-bhutan dossier.

wars.name: Second Anglo-Afghan War
wars.outcome: Treaty of Gandamak, 26 May 1879: Kurram, Pishin, Sibi and the Khyber pass transferred to the British, Afghan foreign policy surrendered; the treaty reaffirmed after Kandahar in 1880.
wars.note: The Durand Line page says 'The British again invaded Afghanistan in 1878' and dates Gandamak 1880; the Gandamak page says 26 May 1879.

wars.name: Third Anglo-Burmese War
wars.outcome: British victory in less than two weeks of November 1885: Mandalay entered on 28 November, monarchy abolished, Upper Burma annexed on 1 January 1886.
wars.note: Resistance continued in northern Burma to 1890.

wars.name: Sikkim expedition of 1888
wars.outcome: 'In 1888 the British sent a military expedition to expel Tibetan forces from Sikkim'; Sikkim remains a British protectorate.
wars.note: The page names no war and no treaty for 1890.

wars.name: Hunza-Nagar Campaign
wars.outcome: Hunza and Nagar 'again subjugated by Anglo-Dogra forces in 1891'.
wars.note: The page names the campaign only through its dated sentence.

wars.name: Anglo-Manipur War

zones.text: the Imphal valley, the Meitei kingdom's core around Kangla

wars.outcome: British victory: Imphal taken on 27 April 1891, Tikendrajit hanged, and on 22 September 1891 'the British placed the young boy Meidingngu Churachand on the throne'; Manipur 'was converted into an Indian princely state subject to British Paramountcy'.
wars.note: Repair sa-06-d. The punitive expedition 'lasted from 31 March to 27 April 1891' after the palace coup of 21 September 1890.

wars.name: Chitral rebellion of 1895
wars.outcome: 'Following a rebellion in 1895, Chitral was transferred to the Malakand Agency in the North-West Frontier Province.'
wars.note: The page does not mention a siege or the relief column.

wars.name: British expedition to Tibet

zones.text: the Chumbi Valley and the road to Gyantse

wars.outcome: British victory: Gyantse (April) and Lhasa (August 1904) reached; the Convention of Lhasa of 7 September 1904, revised by the Anglo-Chinese Convention of 1906, with the Chumbi Valley held until the indemnity was paid, to 8 February 1908.
wars.note: Repair sa-06-d. The expedition 'pressed into Tibetan territories in early December 1903'.

wars.name: Burma campaign

zones.text: the Indian side of the front (reading)

wars.outcome: Japan 'invaded Burma in December 1941' and held much of the colony by the end of 1942; 'In mid-1944, British forces began reversing the Japanese U-Go offensive'; Rangoon 'recaptured in May 1945'. The Raj itself was not conquered.
wars.note: Dates from the Raj and Burma pages; the Imphal and Kohima battles are not on either.

notes:
Written by sa-06-d from ten opened pages (budget: up to 9; British Ceylon and Gilgit Agency are shared with the british-ceylon and kashmir-and-jammu dossiers). CLIOPATRIA ROW: 'British Raj' 1859-1947 is not the Raj. (1) It contains all of Sri Lanka in every year; Ceylon was a Crown colony (British Ceylon page). (2) From 1885 it contains Kashmir and Jammu, whose own row ends in 1884 and resumes in 1947: the kashmir-and-jammu dossier supplies a new 1885-1946 keyframe. (3) It keeps Burma to 1946 although Burma left British India on 1 April 1937. (4) Its 1947 shape is Burma plus Ceylon, not the Raj; the Raj lasted to 14-15 August 1947 and India and Pakistan already have 1947 shapes. (5) It drops 33,400 km2 of the north-east frontier tract in 1939 with no page. (6) The princely states are drawn as direct Raj land, only 561,000 km2 of them being new in 1859. (7) 1943-44 removes Burma and the Andamans; only the Andamans were Raj land. NOT RESOLVED: the princely states other than Hyderabad, Kashmir, Sikkim, Hunza-Nagar and Chitral (the gazetteer cannot name Mysore, Travancore, Baroda, the Punjab states, Kalat, Bahawalpur, Khairpur, Swat and the rest; the region union used covers Rajputana, Kathiawar, Kutch, Malwa and Bundelkhand only and is approximate); Perim, Socotra and the Persian Gulf Residency; Aden ('Part of the Raj from 1858 to 1937, then ... a separate colony'), the Straits Settlements ('Briefly under the Raj, 1858-1867') and British Somaliland ('1884-1898'), which the Raj page lists but Cliopatria does not draw (no events written; they lie outside the 1859-1946 outlines); the Duars of Bhutan (page silent on the 1865 treaty); the 1917-1932 frontier tweaks in the north-east and the Burma-China frontier; the Andaman and Nicobar occupation 1942-1945 and the Manipur front 1944 (pages silent; confidence 1); the Gilgit Agency's exact extent. PAGE CONFLICTS: the Raj page dates the start 2 August 1858 in the infobox and 28 June 1858 in the text; the Durand Line page dates Gandamak 1880, the Gandamak page 26 May 1879; the Gilgit page gives 1 July 1947 for the retrocession and 30 July in the infobox; the Burma page says 'a province of British India on 1 January 1886' while the burma dossier has the Konbaung state ending in November 1885 (the Raj gain is dated November 1885 to agree with it). RULERS: none given. The Raj page's table lists Canning (1 Nov 1858) to Ripon (to 13 Dec 1884) only, and the full viceroy list was not opened within the page budget; a gap-filler should open the list of viceroys. BURMA OVERLAP (for the orchestrator): the british-burma dossier (se-03-x, colony, 1826-1948) draws Burma by itself, while Cliopatria's Raj row, the Burma page and this dossier keep Burma inside British India from 1 January 1886 to 1 April 1937 (the 1937 loss names british-burma). Only one of the two should draw Myanmar in 1886-1936: if british-burma is kept, subtract {'country': 'Myanmar'} from every Raj correction up to 1937 and drop the 1885 gain from the Raj ledger (british-burma has it as a 1886 gain from burma). COUNTERPARTS WITHOUT A DOSSIER: hunza-and-nagar, chitral, and the generic 'Princely states of India'; kingdom-of-sikkim and british-burma exist (kingdom-of-sikkim also records 1861 Darjeeling and Terai annexation, a page this dossier did not open). Gazetteer names used as coordinates: Hunza and Nagar (74.7 E, 36.35 N), Chitral (71.8 E, 35.85 N).
